_meta.purpose: Verified local facts injected into every generated article. Accuracy is a 2026 ranking signal — every fact carries a source. Re-verify dated figures (tariff, subsidy) periodically.

low_speed_exemption.criteria: Top speed 25 km/h or less AND motor 250W or less (continuous rated). BOTH conditions must be met.
low_speed_exemption.insurance_note: Not legally mandated for non-RTO low-speed scooters; voluntary cover is available and recommended. Some interpretations argue third-party cover is still required under the MV Act, and on-ground enforcement varies — phrase as 'confirm with your local RTO' in content, not as black-and-white.
low_speed_exemption.key_nuance: Speed alone is NOT enough. A scooter capped at 25 km/h but fitted with a motor rated above 250W is still classified as a registrable motor vehicle. The exemption checks motor power AND speed. This is the single most common point competitors get wrong — use it as an honest 'buyer beware' angle.
low_speed_exemption.ready_to_ride: Exempt scooters get no registration number; you can ride them as-is the moment you buy. Total on-road cost equals the ex-showroom price.
low_speed_exemption.source: Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR); cross-verified across multiple 2026 sources, June 2026

high_speed.applies_to: FUTURE high-speed / RC two-wheeler vertical — NOT the current low-speed lineup. Keep out of low-speed content.

tricity_regions.note: Central CMVR rules apply identically across all three. State transport departments apply them on the ground, so day-to-day enforcement can differ slightly between UT/Punjab/Haryana. Always direct readers to confirm with their local RTO.

chandigarh_domestic.fixed_charge_note: Approx Rs 20-30 per kW per month plus a small electricity duty per unit
chandigarh_domestic.order: JERC five-year tariff order (FY 2025-26 to 2029-30), first order after CPDL privatisation
chandigarh_domestic.source: Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission (JERC) / Chandigarh Power Distribution Ltd; The Tribune, Oct/Nov 2025

electricity_tariff.local_hook: Chandigarh domestic power (Rs 2.80-3.75 per unit) is materially cheaper than Punjab (Rs 5.40+ per unit). An EV is even cheaper to run inside Chandigarh than across the border in Mohali — a true, ownable, hyper-local content line.

charging_cost.worked_example: At Chandigarh tariff, a ~2-unit full charge costs roughly Rs 12-16 versus Rs 150-200 of petrol for the same distance.
charging_cost.source: Zelio official + EV India guidance; June 2026

pm_e_drive.scheme: PM E-DRIVE (successor to FAME-II), Ministry of Heavy Industries
pm_e_drive.applies_to: REGISTERED high-speed electric two-wheelers with an advanced (lithium-ion) battery, ex-factory price up to Rs 1.5 lakh.
pm_e_drive.deadline: 31 July 2026 for registered e-2Ws; fund-limited (Rs 10,900 crore outlay) and may close earlier if exhausted.
pm_e_drive.low_speed_note: CRITICAL: Low-speed Zelio scooters are CMVR-exempt (unregistered) and frequently lead-acid, so they do NOT qualify for PM E-DRIVE. Do not imply otherwise. The low-speed value proposition is AVOIDED COST (no registration, no road tax, no licence, no mandatory insurance) — not subsidy. Reserve subsidy messaging for the future high-speed vertical only.
pm_e_drive.source: PM E-DRIVE portal (pmedrive.heavyindustries.gov.in) + trade press; June 2026

punjab_state.note: Punjab's own EV policy incentives have been intermittent / not consistently notified. Confirm current live status before relying on it for high-speed-vertical content.

low_speed_current.message: No licence, no registration, no road tax, no mandatory insurance, ride today. Total cost = sticker price. Runs at ~Rs 0.25/km on cheap Chandigarh power.

high_speed_future.message: PM E-DRIVE up to Rs 5,000 (while funds last, till 31 Jul 2026) plus any live Punjab state incentive — for registered, licensed riders.
